candidates.title: A Lawyer’s Fifteen-Year Wager
candidates.rights_reasoning: Project Gutenberg explicitly marks this Chekhov collection as public domain in the United States, covering the included story “The Bet” and its listed translation.
candidates.story_fit_reason: A wealthy banker and a young lawyer make one startling wager, giving an adaptation a clear setting, conflict, time pressure, and two central characters. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/55283?utm_source=openai))
candidates.concern: The English translation is separately credited, so non-U.S. rights should be checked before international publication.

candidates.title: A Couple’s Impossible Christmas Gifts
candidates.rights_reasoning: Project Gutenberg identifies O. Henry’s individual story as public domain in the United States.
candidates.story_fit_reason: A poor young couple secretly sells or sacrifices a treasured possession to buy a gift for the other, creating a compact, emotionally direct episode suitable for simplified English. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/7256?msg=welcome_strangerThis&utm_source=openai))
candidates.concern: The story’s famous twist is culturally familiar, so an adaptation would need a fresh setting or emphasis.

candidates.title: The Signalman’s Dangerous Decision
candidates.rights_reasoning: Project Gutenberg marks the Russian short-story volume as public domain in the United States and lists Vsevolod Garshin’s “The Signal” among its contents.
candidates.story_fit_reason: A single railway worker must decide whether and how to warn an approaching train, providing a concrete physical danger and a straightforward sequence of actions. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/68619?utm_source=openai))
candidates.concern: The source is an anthology rather than an individual story page, and the credited English translation should be checked for the target market.

candidates.title: A Woman Who Borrows a Necklace
candidates.rights_reasoning: Project Gutenberg explicitly marks this anthology as public domain in the United States and lists Guy de Maupassant’s “The Necklace” in its contents.
candidates.story_fit_reason: One woman’s decision to borrow jewelry for a single prestigious evening leads to a sharply focused chain of consequences that can be retold with accessible vocabulary. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10483?utm_source=openai))
candidates.concern: This is a well-known story, so the adaptation should avoid reproducing its exact wording or familiar presentation.

candidates.title: A Stranger Trapped Behind a Door
candidates.rights_reasoning: Project Gutenberg marks the anthology as public domain in the United States and specifically lists Robert Louis Stevenson’s “The Sire de Malétroit’s Door.”
candidates.story_fit_reason: A traveler becomes trapped outside a mysterious door and is forced into an unexpected encounter, giving a short adaptation one location, a small cast, and immediate suspense. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/21964?utm_source=openai))
candidates.concern: The anthology includes editorial material as well as fiction, so the story text should be isolated from the surrounding commentary.
